The following observations were collected during experimentation on a clear sample solution created by dissolving two different inorganic salts in distilled water:
- The sample solution has a pH of around 5.
- Addition of FeCl3 to the sample causes the color of the solution to change to red. No precipitates form during this step.
- Addition of AgNO3 to the sample solution results in a white precipitate.
- This white precipitate partially (but not fully) dissolves in dilute nitric acid.
- When Pb(NO3)2 is added to the supernatant solution of the previous step, a white precipitate forms.

Assuming that all of the above statements are true, which of the following options is correct?
